subject: Low and close, straight on: an older woman's two pale legs on her carpeted staircase, facing down the stairs towards the camera, a black STRYDE strap seated just below EACH kneecap — pointed peaks, the kneecap seated in the notch, chrome slides, the grey lowercase stryde wordmark — her denim skirt hem above, white plimsolls below. Exactly as in the start frame.

camera.movement: Locked off on a small tripod: the camera does not move at all, no pan, no tilt, no push, no drift.

motion: Already walking on the first frame: she walks down the stairs towards the camera, one easy step down with one foot, then the other, about two seconds, steady and sure, starting straight away. She only ever comes down, facing the camera, never turning. Both straps stay exactly as they are — rigid, the same shape, size and wordmark from first frame to last. Everything in frame keeps the exact form, proportion and count it has in the start frame, first frame to last — nothing melts, merges, splits, grows or becomes something else. One small movement, completing inside the clip, subject fully in frame throughout, nothing leaving frame and returning. Mass and momentum in all movement: heavy starts and settles slow, nothing at uniform speed, nothing stops instantly — motions decelerate into a settle or small overshoot; actions travel through the body, weight transferring first, hands arriving last; the skirt hem lags a little; the straps never move; objects drag with friction, never glide.
lighting: Capture characteristics exactly as in the start frame — same tone-mapping, same noise, same colour temperature. No grading change across the clip.
